public_rationale: InfoWorld reported Anthropic's capacity restrictions on March 27, 2026, and CNAS described chip supply constraints on May 7 [e1, e2]. OpenAI acknowledged demand growing faster than capacity on July 29, after the May 19 forecast [e3]. These items support compute supply pressure, but do not show that shortages forced both companies to purchase compute on materially worse terms [e1, e2, e3]. They also do not establish already-negative overall profit margins or subsequent material deterioration caused by those purchases [e1, e2, e3]. Anthropic announced some usage-limit relief on May 6, before the forecast [e4]. That relief establishes neither subsequent margin effects nor a permanent end to shortages [e4]. The evidence therefore does not establish or permanently foreclose the predicted financial sequence for both companies [e1, e2, e3, e4].
limitations: No matched post-publication records connect shortages, worse comparable purchase terms and resulting margin deterioration for both companies.
The evidence does not establish the claimed negative starting margins on a consistent accounting basis.
The claim specifies neither a deadline nor a margin measure or numerical threshold for material damage.
Temporary capacity relief cannot settle this forecast with no stated deadline.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Because not enough compute is being built, Anthropic and OpenAI will pay whatever prices they must for compute, further damaging their already-negative margins.

statement.excerpt: And right now, as I’ve covered, there’s not enough compute being built to keep up with Anthropic or OpenAI’s voracious demands, meaning that they will both be bartering to buy whatever’s available at whatever price it’s available at. This naturally will savage their already-negative margins…

our_interpretation: The asserted shortage is the antecedent: available compute cannot keep pace with the labs' demand.
Whatever price means materially worse purchasing terms forced by scarcity, not literally an unlimited willingness to pay.
Savage means a material deterioration attributable to procurement costs, not an immaterial fluctuation.

Already-negative margins most naturally refers to overall profitability because the preceding gross-margin figures are positive. Net profit margin is a provisional operationalization; the speaker does not specify it.
criteria.support_condition: After publication, both companies face constrained compute supply, purchase capacity on materially worse comparable terms because of that constraint, and experience a material resulting deterioration in consistently measured profit margins.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive completed episode or permanent change establishes that the asserted shortage did not produce the predicted procurement and margin effects. Temporary improvement or mere nonoccurrence cannot defeat an unlimited-horizon forecast.

evidence.publisher: Center for a New American Security
evidence.explanation: The report identifies a supply constraint on compute construction. Together with the company-specific items, it supports the antecedent, not the predicted financial damage.
Anthropic faced demand pressure sufficient to restrict usage. This establishes a capacity constraint, not premium procurement or a subsequent margin decline.

evidence.locator: Section Accelerating inference with GPT‑5.6 Sol, first paragraph
evidence.explanation: OpenAI acknowledges the capacity constraint while discussing its inference infrastructure. The disclosure does not quantify procurement premiums or the resulting effect on profit margins.

evidence.excerpt: removing the peak hours limit reduction
evidence.explanation: Anthropic reports easing a restriction alongside new compute agreements. This qualifies any assumption that shortages cannot ease, but neither establishes adequate total supply nor settles future margins.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated evidence after May 19, 2026 showing that shortages forced both companies to buy comparable compute on materially worse terms and materially worsened their already-negative profit margins. The records must use consistent margin measures and separate procurement effects from other costs. Alternatively, a decisive event must permanently foreclose that sequence.
